text:
maria: Quick heads-up: profiler on canary gpu-5 showing intermittent stalls where the batcher waits ~120ms then we hit an OOM-like failure in the kernel. Seems tied to heavy KV cache copies during batch formation. Seen mainly on long-prefix workloads.
chris: Do you have the perf map + batch sizes? Wondering if the kernel selector is flipping to fallback kernels because of cache footprint.
maria: Snippet from the profiler tail (condensed):
```prof
batcher: formed batch=8 reqs tot_tokens=1420 kv_bytes=1.9G
kernel: chosen=attention_v2_fused_fallback
gpu_mem_free: 600MB -> after alloc fails
```
devon: If kv_bytes ~= 1.9G that's close to our soft-evict watermark. The batcher still uses token_budget=512 per-slot which allows oversized prefetch/kv reservations. We should clamp admission by a kv_estimate, not only token counts.
chris: Agreed. Proposed heuristic: before admit, compute kv_est = prefix_len * avg_kv_per_token; require (kv_est + current_kv_usage) < kv_headroom_bytes. If it fails, try soft-shrink the batch or pick a kernel variant with smaller KV temp buffers (kernel_route).
maria: Quick canary plan: when gpu_free < 1G, force per-request token_budget = min(request_tokens, 256) and route very-heavy-prefix requests to slow-path kernel explicitly. I'll push a patch to test.
devon: Also worth noting: we introduced a perf regression in a1b2c3 where selector started preferring fused kernels for len>1024; fused kernels use bigger per-kv temporaries. That explains why OOMs started appearing under mixed load.
qa-jen: I can run a mixed-prefix load test matrix (short/med/long prefixes) and measure p50/p95/p99 impact. Will report if soft-reduce causes bad p99 regressions.
maria: Deployed quick patch to canary: `batcher/kv_admit.cc` adds kv_est check and reduces admit size 8->6 when headroom low. 30s into canary: no OOMs so far. Median latency +8ms, p99 +40ms on long-prefix heavy flows.
chris: :thumbsup: Good. Next steps: 1) Add kernel-cost model with kv_temp_bytes per kernel variant so selector can prefer low-kv kernels under pressure. 2) Telemetry: add `kv-admit-shed` counter and `kernel-choice-under-kv-pressure` label. 3) Run broader canary across 3 hosts to ensure stability.
sre-bot: deploy: canary updated (maria) — 1 instance rolling, status healthy
maria: I'll open a follow-up PR to add the kernel-cost table + unit tests and create an incident note if the canary remains clean for 1h. Thanks folks.
